summary: OS language pack install race blocks Passport for Work enrollment during provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
During recent mass imaging runs, devices with additional OS language packs applied in the provisioning sequence intermittently fail to complete Passport for Work (Windows Hello for Business) enrollment. Failure typically occurs late in OOBE/Autopilot before the user-first login. Affected devices remain in 'Provisioning: Partially configured' state and cannot authenticate against corporate resources until manual remediation.

Impact:
- ~6% of devices imaged in the last 48 hours failed automatic Hello/Passport enrollment and were flagged for manual follow-up by Depot.
- Blocker for new hires whose laptops were imaged in the affected batches — delays onboarding.
- Pattern observed across two laptop SKUs and multiple AD sites in us-east.

Environment:
- Imaging pipeline: Autopilot + MDT-derived OS image (Windows 11 22H2 baseline) + post-image provisioning PowerShell (imaging-scripts repo).
- Additional language packs installed via DISM /Add-Package step in provisioning script (es-ES, fr-FR in recent manifests).
- MDM: Intune (company portal enrollment enabled).

Steps to reproduce (intermittent):
1) Boot Autopilot-provisioned device with the current Golden image.
2) Provisioning script runs: installs drivers, applies updates, then calls Install-LanguagePacks (DISM) with two language packs in parallel (script currently spawns parallel jobs).
3) Immediately after language pack step, script triggers Intune enrollment and Windows Hello for Business CSP policies.
4) Device sometimes fails Passport enrollment with CSP status failures and event log errors (see Observed behavior).

Observed behavior / logs:
- Event Viewer (Applications and Services Logs -> Microsoft -> Windows -> HelloForBusiness/Operational): multiple errors with EventID 5640 and 5641 describing "CSP provisioning failed" and "Key attestation challenge timed out".
- System: Event ID 153 (User Device Registration) with error code 0x8007000D on affected runs.
- SetupDiag/OOBE logs: OOBE\Provisioning-ProvisioningDiagnostics.log shows: "LanguagePackInstall: Completed with warnings; Registry applets reloaded" followed quickly by "PassportForWork: Enrollment aborted - dependency not ready".
- Imaging script logs (pipelines/imaging-scripts/logs): a pattern where Install-LanguagePacks completes within 12s and enrollment starts within 5s of completion on failing runs.
- No persistent 5xx platform errors; network and PKI logs show normal CA reachability.

Hypothesis / investigation notes:
- Primary hypothesis: race between language pack installation (which triggers package registration and some localized service restarts) and Passport/Hello CSP startup sequence. Parallelized DISM jobs are likely causing transient service restarts or package registration events that the Hello CSP interprets as "dependency not ready," causing enrollment to abort and mark the device as incomplete.
- Reproduction more common when two language packs are installed concurrently or the disk I/O on NVMe is saturated (observed in Dell XPS tasks where disk queue depth peaked).
- Workaround that appeared effective: serializing language pack installation and introducing a 30s wait+LPK cache refresh before triggering enrollment reduces failure rate to ~0.5% in the lab.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Imaging team rolled a hotfix to imaging-scripts (branch hotfix/languagepack-serialize) that changes Install-LanguagePacks to run sequentially and adds a 45s pause + call to Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers | Out-Null before starting enrollment. Deployed to one depot batch with immediate improvement. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/imaging-scripts/pull/412

Next steps / action items:
1) Reproduce reliably in lab by running parallel DISM installs on the same SKU under IO stress; capture ETL (Microsoft-Windows-WindowsHelloForBusiness) and DISM traces. Owner: Raj Patel. Target: 2026-03-15.
2) If reproduced, engage Windows platform team (via internal WinPlatform channel) to determine whether Hello CSP should tolerate transient package registration events or expose a retryable error path. Owner: Raj Patel.
3) Keep hotfix (serialize language packs) in imaging pipeline until upstream resolution. Owner: Imaging team (Elena Gomez).
4) Add explicit enrollment verification step in provisioning orchestration: if Passport enrollment fails, retry enrollment twice with 60s backoff before marking device for manual work. Owner: Automation engineers.
5) Document the problem and hotfix in Confluence (Provisioning Runbook v3). Owner: Maya Chen.

Related artifacts:
- Pipeline logs: s3://imaging-logs/2026-03-09/batch-17/*.log (internal access only).
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/imaging-scripts/pull/412
- Runbook page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IT/Provisioning+Runbook+v3

Status: investigation in progress. Hotfix deployed to one depot batch reduced failures; full rollout paused pending lab repro and Windows platform guidance.
